messages.author: 823dbccdc15c7f4a
messages.subject: align.plots ggExtra for consecutive plots
parts:
Hi,
I use the align.plots function from ggExtra sucessfully to align plots
whose
vertical axis is identical in one figure.
However I would like to create a presentation where pictures in
succession have
identical sizes. Then they would only differ in the color of the dots,
because they
display different factors on successive plots on the same underlying
data, without
irritating the viewer by jumping around.

How could I do this?
a)
One possibility is creating the plots multiple times where I exchange
the labels to some
dummy value. The resulting plots should have the same dimensions and
then I can
exchange the labels by hand in a drawing program. Not very elegant.
b)
splitting a pdf created with align.plots into identical subplots.
c)
coding something like align.plots but saving each subfigure to a
separate pdf.

Are there more possibilities?

thank you very much in advance,
ido

limits on all scales. A reproducible example is likely to yield

messages.author: 823dbccdc15c7f4a
messages.subject: Re: align.plots ggExtra for consecutive plots
parts:
On Aug 15, 1:50 pm, Hadley Wickham <had...@rice.edu> wrote:
> You should be able to do what you want by manually specifying the
> limits on all scales. A reproducible example is likely to yield
> better answers.

Thank you very much for your answer. I already gave my presentation
and these minor aesthaetic problems of course did not hurt.

My problem was that the plot canvas has different sizes/positions
depending on the size of the legend - which is determined by the
factor name.
align.plots successfully aligns the panels on the same plot.
I would have liked to split this aligned plot now - with the same size
of the panel - into separate files. Then the plots would not jump
around during
the presentation where I say something like: "at1" does not correlate
with the increase /next slide/ but "longAttribute" does correlate.

Example:
library("ggplot2")
library("ggExtra")
df <- data.frame(ids=LETTERS[1:10],value=1:10,at1=rep(c("A","B"),
5),longAttributeName=rep(c("C","D")))
pat1 <- ggplot(df, aes(ids,value)) + geom_point() +
scale_y_continuous("measured",limits=c(0,10)) +
aes(colour=factor(at1))
plat <- ggplot(df, aes(ids,value)) + geom_point() +
scale_y_continuous("measured",limits=c(0,10)) +
aes(colour=factor(longAttributeName))
pat1
plat
align.plots(pat1 + opts(axis.text.x = theme_blank())+xlab(""), plat)

thank you very much,
ido
